messages.subject: Include NA values in fscores
parts: I'm estimating factor scores using fscores(). I have some rows with completely missing data, which I remove using removeEmptyRows = TRUE. However, after using fscores(), I'd like to re-merge the estimated factor scores with the rest of my data. This is difficult because the rows of the fscores() matrix do not align with the original matrix. Would it be possible to add an option to restore the rows that were removed with N/A's? Alternatively, would it be possible to permit data to contain in ID column that could be used to rejoin the data?

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Include NA values in fscores
parts:
Sorry for the delay; work life/home life is insane right now. This is a good question that I hadn't considered when adding the remove rows option. I suppose it would make sense to store the row-numbers of the rows that were completely removed (or perhaps more naturally, the rows that were retained) in the estimated object, which can then be extracted via extract.mirt(). I'll open a feature on Github to add this into the next major release, which I'm planning for next week.

Phil

messages.subject: Re: Include NA values in fscores
parts:
Done. This now works as follows:

library(mirt)
Science[1:2, ] <- NA
mod <- mirt(Science, 1, technical = list(removeEmptyRows=TRUE))

rowID <- extract.mirt(mod, 'rowID')
head(rowID)

fs <- data.frame(ID=rowID, fscores(mod))
Science$ID <- 1:nrow(Science)

merged <- merge(Science, fs, by = 'ID', all = TRUE)
head(merged)

Which gives:

  ID Comfort Work Future Benefit         F1
1  1      NA   NA     NA      NA         NA
2  2      NA   NA     NA      NA         NA
3  3       3    2      2       3 -0.8840632
4  4       3    2      2       3 -0.8840632
5  5       3    4      4       1  0.7585119
6  6       4    4      3       3  0.6716056

Phil

Could you also add an argument to fscores() to include the rowID in one go? For example, `rowID = "ID"` would add the ID numbers to the fscores output with the name "ID".

One other thing that would be great is if mirt() and the other model calls had a `rowID` argument  specifying the variable in `data` to use as the rowID, rather than the row numbers.

messages.subject: Re: Include NA values in fscores
parts:
Hi Brenton,

I'd rather keep the data input argument a little neater and contain only the item response observations, though I'm not opposed to adding a rowID variable to mirt() and friends to change the default 1:N vector that is created and tracked internally. Would that be sufficient for your needs? I could also add an include_rowID argument to fscores() as well to column-bind this ID vector to the factor scores as well.

Phil
